WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r5.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r5.claim: ʿIkrima agrees with Sufyān that the period was seven years.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r6.claim: Muqātil b. Sulaymān says Joseph remained imprisoned for twelve years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان (¬1): حبس يوسف اثني عشرة سنة (¬2)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r7.claim: The governor agreed to his wife's request and imprisoned Joseph despite knowing he was innocent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r7.anchor: وفي هذه الآية بيان أن العزيز أطاع زوجته في حبس يوسف، بعد علمه ببراءته، موافقة لها،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r8.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r8.claim: The commentators say God made the imprisonment a purification for Joseph from his desire for the woman and an expiation for his lapse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r8.anchor: وذكر المفسرون (¬3) أن الله تعالى جعل ذلك الحبس [تطهيرا] (¬4) ليوسف من همه بالمرأة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r9.claim: God left the period unspecified to honor scholars and direct people to them to solve interpretive difficulties.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r9.anchor: وذكر ابن الأنباري أن الله تعالى أبهم الحين هاهنا، إرادة لتكرمة العلماء ورفعا لأقدارهم؛

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r2.claim: After seeing signs of Joseph's innocence, the ruler and his companions decided to imprison him until the public blame stopped.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r2.anchor: للعزيز وأصحابه { من بعد ما رأوا الآيات }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r3.claim: The ruler's wife said Joseph had exposed her by telling people she had tried to seduce him, so she wanted him imprisoned until gossip ended.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r3.anchor: إن هذا العبد فضحني في الناس

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:35/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:35/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:35/r1.claim: Aziz’s household sought to protect its reputation and conceal the affair; the woman wanted to punish Joseph’s disobedience by blaming the slave and imprisoning him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:35/r1.anchor: Aziz’in ailesini temize çıkarıp zevâhiri kurtarmak ve olayı örtbas etmek, istediği anlaşılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:35/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:35/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:35/r2.claim: Despite evidence that Joseph was innocent and the woman guilty, Aziz and his associates chose to imprison him for a time.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:35/r2.anchor: bütün delillerin Yûsuf’un günahsız, kadının ise suçlu olduğunu göstermesine rağmen Aziz ve arkadaşları, Yûsuf’un bir süre zindana atılmasını uygun gördüler

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Joseph’s imprisonment begins another trial: his powerful hosts knew the reality but judged a short prison term would silence gossip and lessen Zelicha’s infatuation by keeping him away.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they deemed it appropriate to send him to jail for some time. They must have thought that in this way people would stop gossiping about the whole issue

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The signs are evidence that Joseph was innocent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The word “signs” here refer to the evidence of Joseph’s innocence.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Aziz and his relatives knew Joseph was blameless and Zelicha was entirely at fault.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: ‘Azīz and his relatives fully understood that he was not at fault. It was Zelicha who was entirely at fault.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: To avoid embarrassment, they proposed imprisoning Joseph for a while.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: to save evade embarrassment they proposed to imprison Joseph (sws) for some time.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: They expected Zelicha's infatuation and public interest to fade, leaving people to think Joseph was guilty and punished.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: people too would loose interest in this whole incident.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Masters had unrestricted power over enslaved people, so Aziz could readily send Joseph to prison.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The masters of those times had unlimited authority over their slaves.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Aziz's government office and rank in the royal guard would have let him overcome any obstacle to imprisonment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: a person like him who was a government official and also a dignitary of the royal guard would have easily overcome it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: This begins another trial; although people might deem it the hardest, Joseph desired it because faith and character mattered most.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: since faith and character occupied the real importance, he actually desired in fact prayed for this scenario in contrast with the previous one.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p234/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p234/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p234/r1.claim: The opening lexical notes define trade, entreaty as gentle request, seeking marriage, locking, tearing cloth, master or chief, and imprisonment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p234/r1.anchor: المراودة الطلب برفق ولين القول، والرود التأني يقال

AKHFASH:v1p397/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p397/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p397/r3.claim: The emphatic nūn in ليسجننه is licensed because the clause can host an interrogative, as in asking which of them will take someone.
AKHFASH:v1p397/r3.anchor: وقال {ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين} فادخل النون في هذا الموضع لان هذا موضع تقع فيه "أي"

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r3.claim: In لئن زرته ما يقبل منك and لئن فعلت ما فعل, the negative clause means that the person will not accept or do it, rather than a simple past report.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r3.anchor: لئن زرته ما يقبل منك وقال لئن فعلت ما فعل يريد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r9.claim: Verbs of knowledge and supposition can take an oath-like lām and nūn, as Labid's line and Sībawayh's examples with علمت and أظن show.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r10.claim: Sībawayh treats the lām in ليسجننه as lām of beginning: بدا لهم opens a thought, as in ظهر لهم أهذا أفضل أم هذا, analogous to علمت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/r10.anchor: لأنه موضع ابتداء ألا ترى أنك لو قلت بدا لهم أيهم

BURHAN:v4p58/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p58/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p58/r4.claim: Joseph's rescue is attributed to God, while his imprisonment is attributed to the women, although God caused it: mercy is ascribed to Him and hardship to them.
BURHAN:v4p58/r4.anchor: تأمل قوله ﴿ فصرف عنه كيدهن ﴾ 3 فاضافه إلى نفسه حيث صرفه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r1.claim: The explanation of الشرجب as الطويل does not mean the word signals its synonym: its meaning is unknown before explanation, and explaining it simply identifies the synonym.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنك لا تفسر الشرجب حتى يكون معناه مجهولا عند السامع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r2.claim: Rhetorical merit lies in the way a speaker establishes an intended meaning, not in changing the meaning itself; paraphrase and direct wording can share a referent yet differ in force.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r3.claim: Metonymy asserts generosity through its sign, كثرة رماد القدر, so the claim comes with evidence and is more forceful than stating كثرة القرى directly.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r3.anchor: أثبت كثرة القرى بإثبات شاهدها ودليلها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r4.claim: Metaphor is stronger than literal comparison because calling a man a lion asserts identity; the image of advancing one foot and withdrawing the other also proves hesitation more forcefully than naming it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r4.anchor: السبب في أن كانت الاستعارة أبلغ من الحقيقة أنك إذا ادعيت للرجل أنه أسد بالحقيقة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p324/r5.claim: The image of advancing one foot and withdrawing the other establishes hesitation more forcefully than saying directly that the person is hesitant.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r1.claim: Nazm is the arrangement of syntactic meanings, not a property residing in words; people miss its differences because they misunderstand what it is.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r1.anchor: حسبوه شيئا غير توخي معاني النحو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r2.claim: No grammatical form has merit everywhere: its advantage depends on its position, context, and degree of use, so a familiar device can be excellent in one phrase and ordinary elsewhere.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r2.anchor: ندعي المزية لكل ما ندعيها له من معاني النحو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r4.claim: These subtle rhetorical advantages are difficult to teach; the listener needs receptivity, taste, and a faculty that can sense differences in the placement of words in prose and poetry.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p394/r4.anchor: ويكون له ذوق وقريحة يجد لهما

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r1.claim: Ḥīn means a span of time, short or long; the related verb can mean to stay somewhere or for a time to approach.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r1.anchor: الحين : الزمان قليله وكثيره . ويقال : أحينت بالمكان ، إذا أقمت به حينا . وحان حين كذا ، أي : قرب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r2.claim: A poem illustrates the phrase “its time has not yet come.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r2.anchor: وأنشدوا : - وإن سلوي عن جميل لساعة … من الدهر ما حانت ولا حان حينها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r3.claim: One Qur'anic sense of ḥīn is six months.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r3.anchor: أحدها : ستة أشهر ، ومنه قوله تعالى في إبراهيم : ﴿ تؤتي أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r4.claim: Another sense is the end of allotted lifespans or terms of enjoyment.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r4.anchor: والثاني : منتهى الآجال ، ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r5.claim: A third sense is hours or specified parts of the day.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r5.anchor: والثالث : الساعات ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الروم : ^ ( فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون . وله الحمد في السموات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r6.claim: A fourth sense is an unspecified time, as in the promise that the news will be known later.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r6.anchor: والرابع : وقت منكر ، ومنه قوله تعالى في ص : ^ ( ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r7.claim: A fifth sense is forty years; some exegetes fold this into the preceding category of unspecified time.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r7.anchor: والخامس : أربعون سنة ، ومنه قوله تعالى : ^ ( هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر ) ^ . وألحقه قوم بالقسم الذي قبله

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r8.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r8.claim: Some add a sixth sense, three days, to the verse about Thamud being told to enjoy life until a time.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r8.anchor: وألحق قوم قسما سادسا فقالوا : والحين : ثلاثة أيام ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الذاريات : ^ ( وفي ثمود إذ قيل لهم تمتعوا حتى حين )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r9.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r9.claim: Some add midday, or the interval between evening prayers, as another sense; a verifier includes it under hours.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r9.anchor: أحدها : نصف النهار ، ومنه قوله تعالى : ^ ( ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r10.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r10.claim: Some say Joseph was imprisoned for five years, assigning that duration to “until a time.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r10.anchor: والثاني : خمس سنين . ( ومنه قوله تعالى ) ^ ( ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r11.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r11.claim: Some interpret “until a time” as the start of fighting on the day of Badr; the author classifies this and the five-year view as unspecified time.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r11.anchor: والثالث : ابتداء القتال يوم بدر ، ومنه قوله تعالى : ^ ( فتول عنهم حتى حين ) ^ . وهذان القسمان داخلان في قسم الوقت المنكر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r12.claim: The verse itself does not supply the endpoints: Joseph's prison term is known from his release, and the turning away from polytheists from the later order to fight.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p254/r12.anchor: وإنما علمنا نهاية سجن يوسف ، بوقت خروجه ، ونهاية الإعراض عن المشركين ، بوقت الأمر بقتالهم . ولم يستفد ذلك من الآي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f1.claim: An oath on an unfulfilled, nonnegative action takes lām and an emphatic nūn, light or heavy.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f1.anchor: فإذا حلفت على فعل غير منفي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f2.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f2.claim: Al-Khalīl treats emphatic nūn as attaching to lām just as lām attaches in إن كان لصالحا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f2.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن النون تلزم اللام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f3.claim: Verbs carrying oath meaning, such as أقسم and أشهد, license the same lām-and-nūn construction.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f3.anchor: أشياء فيها معنى اليمين يجري الفعل بعدها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f4.claim: For an action already completed, an oath takes lām alone, not nūn; Arabs say والله لفعلت and والله لكذبت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f4.anchor: الفعل قد وقع وحلفت عليه لم تزد على اللام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f5.claim: A negative oath preserves its negation; Arabs may omit لا while still intending it, as in والله أفعل ذاك أبدا meaning والله لا أفعل.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f6.speaker: الشاعر
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f6.claim: An unnamed poet’s فلا والله تهبط تلعة illustrates the negative oath form.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f7.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f7.claim: Al-Khalīl says أقسمت عليك إلا فعلت and لما فعلت are requests modeled on نشدتك الله, though expected oath wording is لتفعلن.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f7.anchor: لأنهم شبهوه بنشدتك الله إذ كان فيه معنى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f8.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f8.claim: An initial لَتَفْعَلُنَّ carries an unspoken oath; the same construction applies to the independent clause ليسجننه in 12:35.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f8.anchor: إذا جاءت مبتدأة ليس قبلها ما يحلف به

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f10.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f10.claim: Al-Khalīl rejects والله تفعل for positive future because it could be confused with والله لا تفعل; nūn distinguishes oath future from ongoing action.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f20.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f20.speaker: لبيد
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f20.claim: Labīd’s لتأتين منيتي and examples after علم and أظن show these verbs can introduce the oath-like emphatic construction.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f20.anchor: كما قال قد علمت لعبد الله خير منك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f21.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f21.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f21.claim: Sībawayh treats ليسجننه as a fresh clause at a point of initiation, with the emphatic oath understood; بدا لهم أيهم أفضل demonstrates the clause boundary.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأفعالفيالقسم)#491/f21.anchor: لأنه موضع ابتداء ألا ترى أنك
